text:
alex chen: Ran a long-run profile on the FP8 path for the 32k-context chat workload overnight. Noticed recurring TTFT spikes tied to a KV handoff window when requests cross device boundaries. flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/2033141592 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria gonzalez: ugh. is it prefill or decode that blows up? or the kvcache eviction? :thinking:

alex chen: Main tail is in the kernel_selector + kvcache eviction + memcpy stack. Spikes correspond to mixed-quant microbatches where some sequences take the FP8 calibrated kernel and others fall back to the slower dequant copy path. Looks like runtime toggling the kernel variant mid-batch causes branching penalties + extra host<->device copies.

kevin park: that matches my hypothesis — calibration metadata is non-uniform across the batch so choose() flips variants. Cheap to pick correct kernel when homogeneous, but expensive when we patch in a different quant-mode mid-microbatch. Also saw increased L2 cache thrash on the GPU.

jess taylor: could be a scheduling/batching heuristic problem. If the microbatcher groups by arrival time only, we mix calibrated+uncalibrated. Two quick ideas: 1) tag microbatches with quant-signature and prefer homogeneous grouping; 2) add a fast-path that pins a kernel variant for the prefill->decode handoff window to avoid mid-flight switching.

alex chen: ran a repro with perf and recorded call stacks:

```
perf record -g -- ./redwood_runtime --model redwood-rlhf-fp8 --ctx 32768 --concurrency 4 --warmup 50
# top stacks: kernel_selector::choose + kvcache::evict + memcpy
# hotspot: choose() spending ~22% when mixed batches present
```

kevin park: can we avoid memcpy by keeping dequant buffer resident? i.e., pre-alloc a fallback dequant slab per-device and avoid repeated malloc/free during handoff. Also calibration state lookup should be O(1) per sequence, not per-token.

jess taylor: agree. also try increasing microbatch grouping window slightly (e.g., from 2ms -> 6ms) to let the batching layer assemble homogeneous groups. Might hurt tail TPS but reduce TTFT variance. This is a classic TTFT vs TPS tradeoff.

alex chen: launching three short canaries to measure impact:
- experiment A: disable runtime kernel toggling (force single kernel variant per-queue)
- experiment B: dequant slab pinned per-device + avoid host copies on handoff
- experiment C: larger grouping window (2ms -> 6ms) + quant-signature grouping

deploy-bot: Canary started: eng-runtime/canary/2033141592-A (A=force-kernel), eng-runtime/canary/2033141592-B, eng-runtime/canary/2033141592-C

maria gonzalez: what metrics to watch? baseline TTFT median 110ms, 95th 420ms, TPS 8.6k. We want to keep median ~<=125ms and not lose >10% TPS if possible. Also track GPU memcpy throughput and kernel occupancy.

alex chen: early results after 15m:
- A (force-kernel): median TTFT 120ms, 95th 260ms (big improvement), TPS -8%
- B (pinned slab): median TTFT 115ms, 95th 230ms, TPS -3%
- C (grouping): median TTFT 130ms, 95th 270ms, TPS -5%

kevin park: interesting, B looks best compromise. suggests the memcpy/alloc churn was the dominant cost, not kernel perf itself. Also shows the calibration mismatch cost is mostly amortized by avoiding copies.

jess taylor: can we combine B + mild grouping? B + 3ms window might give median ~112ms and TPS -2% vs baseline. Worth a small perf test.

alex chen: will run a 2h run for B + 3ms grouping. Also adding an instrumentation flag to kernel_selector to log variant flips per-microbatch so we can quantify how often the handoff happens.

maria gonzalez: add regression alert on 95th TTFT > 300ms for the next rollout so we get early warnings.

alex chen: noted. I'll open a follow-up issue with perf artifacts + stack dumps and assign action items: pin dequant slab (kevin), batcher grouping change (jess), selector flip counter (alex).

kevin park: small implementation note — use cudaHostAlloc with portable flag to avoid page migration thrash on multi-GPU hosts.

jess taylor: will prototype grouping change and add a config toggle. keeping default conservatively low so existing SLAs unaffected.

deploy-bot: Canary eng-runtime/canary/2033141592-B completed: success (metrics within thresholds).

alex chen: thanks everyone. Next steps: merge B + 3ms grouping to staging, run 24h soak, then promote. I'll attach the flamegraphs and perf.data in the issue.
